text: Verdict: valid. Domain: real sequences (a_n), (b_n) indexed by n in N, with a, b in R, convergence in the usual metric. Conditions: epsilon > 0 is arbitrary but fixed; 'eventually' means 'for all sufficiently large n'; the threshold N may depend on epsilon. Proof: Given epsilon > 0, a_n -> a gives N_a such that |a_n - a| < epsilon/2 for all n >= N_a, and b_n -> b gives N_b such that |b_n - b| < epsilon/2 for all n >= N_b. Let N = max(N_a, N_b). For n >= N, |(a_n + b_n) - (a + b)| = |(a_n - a) + (b_n - b)| <= |a_n - a| + |b_n - b| < epsilon/2 + epsilon/2 = epsilon. Hence for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that for all n >= N the sum error is < epsilon; therefore a_n + b_n -> a + b. Defect: none.
